figures.alt: Brick commercial taproom under construction with framed bar, plumbing, and ceiling services
figures.caption: A taproom fit-out has to coordinate the bar, plumbing, electrical, ventilation, floor protection, and finish sequence. The visible room comes together only after those systems have a workable route.

figures.alt: Brewery production room with sealed floor, linear trench drain, equipment pad, and plumbing rough-in
figures.caption: Brewery production depends on a floor that can handle cleaning water. Drain location, slope, durable finishes, and equipment-pad coordination need to be resolved before brewing equipment arrives.

figures.alt: Commercial accessible-restroom rough-in with fixture backing, plumbing connections, and clear floor area
figures.caption: Taproom occupancy affects restroom capacity, routes, and fixture layout. Accessibility is most reliable when the required room geometry and rough-in are coordinated before finishes close the walls.
